proposal: The Mandate recommends making performance appraisal meaningful (it criticizes ratings clustered at the top, wants political executives to take an active role in supervising career appraisals, and wants managers judged on how they rate staff) and reissuing the 2018 order (EO 13839) that shortened improvement periods, sped discipline, required reminders to supervisors about expiring probationary periods, and barred settlements that alter personnel records. status_summary: OPM finalized two appraisal rules: the Senior Executive Service rule (published 2025-09-15, effective 2025-10-15) and the General Schedule rule (published 2026-07-07, effective 2026-08-06, with some summary-level provisions required from 2027-01-01). Both let OPM set a distribution of top ratings; the General Schedule rule also drops Level 2 and removes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures as agreements expire. An OPM memo of 2026-09-21 caps combined Level 4 and 5 ratings at 40 percent of each covered career population for appraisal periods ending 2026-09-30, with waivers up to 50 percent. On probationary employees, OPM published a final rule on 2026-08-03 (effective 2026-09-02) setting a limited OPM appeal process after EO 14284 had made the prior MSPB procedures inoperative. Most removal-side changes resembling EO 13839 (a 30-day improvement period, removal as the default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, limits on settlements that alter records) remain in a joint OPM and MSPB proposed rule of 2026-07-02 that was not final as of 2026-10-13, though the MSPB separately finalized a rule (effective 2026-10-05) ending the requirement to weigh all 12 Douglas factors in misconduct penalty reviews. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB has not happened; OPM-run appeals now handle reductions in force and probationary terminations.

timeline.event: OPM memo on revocation of EO 14003 tells agencies to review discipline and performance policies changed under that order and return to first-term policies, with a report due 2025-03-07; it does not itself reinstate EO 13839.

OPM final rule, Assuring Responsive and Accountable Federal Executive Management (effective 2025-10-15), lets OPM set forced distribution of SES rating levels and removes a diversity-related appraisal factor.
OPM announces a final suitability rule extending suitability actions to serious post-appointment misconduct in covered positions (date from OPM news listing; Federal Register citation not reviewed).

OPM's Suitability and Fitness final rule is published in the Federal Register (91 FR 39361, effective 2026-07-30), allowing suitability actions based on serious post-appointment conduct of current employees; this is the Federal Register text of the rule announced 2026-06-29.

OPM and MSPB publish proposed rule Promoting Employee Accountability: default 30-day improvement opportunity, removal as default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, MSPB to drop the Douglas factors, limits on settlement terms that alter records, no official time to represent colleagues in covered proceedings.

OPM final rule on performance appraisal for General Schedule, prevailing rate and certain other employees (effective 2026-08-06): drops Level 2, allows OPM-set distribution of upper ratings, removes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures, requires a supervisory critical element.
OPM releases a Performance Management Officer manual and updated appraisal-system approval form to help agencies implement the General Schedule rule.

OPM final rule Streamlining Probationary and Trial Period Appeals (91 FR 49072, effective 2026-09-02) creates a limited OPM-adjudicated appeal process for probationary and trial-period terminations, replacing MSPB procedures that EO 14284 (2025-04-24) had made inoperative; a correction and technical amendment was published 2026-08-25.

MSPB publishes a final rule (91 FR 56549, effective 2026-10-05) ending the requirement to weigh all 12 Douglas factors when reviewing penalties in misconduct-based adverse actions, replacing it with a case-by-case totality-of-circumstances reasonableness test.
OPM reopens the Promoting Employee Accountability comment period (to 2026-09-29) limited to new OPM data and a report published 2026-08-27.

OPM memo sets FY2026 standardized distribution: combined Level 4 and 5 ratings capped at 40 percent per covered population (first year for career General Schedule employees), with waivers up to 50 percent, plus awards guidance steering at least 60 percent of bonus pools to Level 4 and 5.

title: Strengthen appraisal ratings and speed removal of poor performers

The MSPB Douglas factors rule was read from its Federal Register API abstract; how it relates to the joint OPM and MSPB proposal was not confirmed from its text.
